newsitem.title: POLAND: IMI SEES WARSAW BOURSE AT 18,500 YEAR-END.
newsitem.headline: IMI SEES WARSAW BOURSE AT 18,500 YEAR-END.

text.p: IMI Sigeco UK Ltd, part of the IMI Group, sees the Warsaw Stock Exchange ending this year at 18,500 points, IMI said in a report dated March 14.
The Warsaw bourse's main WIG index was at 16,687.1 points at the time of the report and closed at 15,652.7 points on Thursday.
"Our current forecast for the year-end level of the market is 18,500 which...would put the total market on an estimated P/E of 12.1 times 1997 earnings and 10.8 times 1998 earnings," the report said.
IMI said the 18,500-point forecast would represent capital appreciation of 29 percent over the year in the local currency and 9.5 percent in dollar terms.

It said the market should move sideways over the next few months as investors concentrated on this year's several privatisations and primary issues, and that by mid-summer investors would be focused on the coming parliamentary vote.

IMI said it saw 1997 earnings per share growth of 15 percent for the overall market, kept down by slower growth from the banking sector, and earnings growth of 14 percent in 1998, the latter implying real progress of about two to four percent.

It said investment, consumer demand and industrial and construction output growth would help fuel profit growth this year, as would mergers and acquisitions in the food, brewing, construction and banking sectors.
IMI said investors should buy Agros, BRE, Farm Food , Gorazdze , Irena , Optimus , Polifarb Cieszyn , Polfa Kutno and WBK .
It said they should hold BFK , Elektrim , Exbud , Wedel and Zywiec.
